c2_bad.why: A 320-480px inline-on-wide-screens drawer with a tvOS focusSection variant. The artifact is an iOS modal .sheet on a 390pt phone; nothing in the task concerns a side panel. Carried over unchanged from c1, where it was explicitly recorded as ignored.
Streaks has no photos, camera or thumbnails; the sheet is name, icon grid, frequency and reminder time. Selected at lexical 0.02 solely for 'required coverage: large touch targets'.

Nothing in the Add Habit sheet is draggable, and the record was chosen for 'required coverage: keyboard navigation and focus order' - a concept the pre-registered expectation lists as forbidden for this task, because 'keyboard' here means the on-screen IME, not a hardware keyboard. It re-imports the exact misreading that made c1 harmful.
Hover/pressed/focus/disabled state tokens on a touch-only sheet; the c1 run rejected the equivalent pick (a11y-nontext-contrast for the focus ring) for the same reason.

touch.safe_areas, one of the two critical concepts, is listed as uncovered (mobile-safe-areas and cta-sticky-bar dropped by the cap), and safeAreaInset is the SwiftUI mechanism the actual fix used to pin the primary button above the keyboard. mobile-keyboard-ime covers the intent ('keep the primary action reachable while the keyboard is open') but not the inset/home-indicator mechanics; touch.thumb_reach and process.safe_modification are also uncovered.

why: c2 fixes the mode (refactor, not create) and puts mobile-keyboard-ime in the bundle - the one record that states this task's fix (return key Next/Done, scroll the focused field above the keyboard, keep the primary action reachable, dismiss on tap outside), which in c1 the implementer had to dig out of the raw search himself - and it drops the ecommerce PDP core record and the failed poster/grid/sticky-bar direction; four of eight slots are still irrelevant filler, one of which re-imports the forbidden hardware-keyboard reading.
